profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC3 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC3 is a 67,038-square-foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's larger campus in Data Center Alley, Loudoun County. The operator does not publish this building's power capacity. Based on DC2, a representative campus facility described as 118,446 square feet with a minimum cabinet density of 4 kVA, this building's floor area suggests a power draw in a lower range than DC2, but the actual IT load capacity remains unspecified. The facility is certified for HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High workloads.

DC3 sits in the greatest documented concentration of data center space on earth, roughly 10 million square feet across Loudoun County, anchored by AOL's Dulles Technology Center from 1997 and Equinix's own DC1 and DC2 buildings from the late 1990s. Equinix operates the Ashburn campus as a top-three internet peering exchange market on the US East Coast, offering colocation, interconnection services, and metro connectivity. Among Virginia's 326 mapped data center facilities, only 23 operators publish power figures; Virginia's total published capacity stands at 1,375 megawatts, but DC3's own figure does not appear in that total because Equinix does not disclose it.

The limiting factor for assessing DC3's relevance to AI scaling is the absence of published power. Without that number, or a reliable method to infer it from floor area and typical rack density, the facility's actual compute capacity cannot be determined. Ashburn's historical role as the birthplace of commercial internet infrastructure and its current status as a peering hub suggest strong existing fiber connectivity, a prerequisite for AI workloads, but whether DC3 itself is built, sized, and provisioned for dense accelerator deployments remains unknown from published sources.
